A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Content can be matched despite substantial restructuring and replacement of experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original maze-planning, D4RL locomotion, CompBench and conditional ImageNet experiments, including search-efficiency and double-verifier results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds BFS ablations and comparisons, policy-distillation outcomes, sensitivity analyses and reward-hacking evaluations.

M1.justification: v2 replaces rounded-allocation BFS-Resampling/BFS-Pruning with configurable tempering, path-based scoring and resampling, selecting Increase/Max/SSP (Section 4.1.1; Appendix D.1). It also revises DFS buffer selection and implements policy distillation through TTS-generated action labels and fine-tuning. Recurrent local search and the double-verifier principle already existed in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds ImageReward prompt-based preference evaluation. Maze coverage contracts from Giant and Ultra to the retained 20-by-20 Ultra layout, now unnamed. The spatial/numeracy CompBench evaluations reported in v1 are absent from v2, which retains attribute-binding examples. D4RL locomotion and conditional ImageNet remain; the distillation study reuses D4RL.

E2.justification: v2 adds FK-steering, DAS, TreeG and SVDD to image-generation comparisons, TFG/DAS to maze and D4RL comparisons, and DPPO to the distillation comparison. CompBench additionally compares DFS with BFS. The D4RL table removes CQL and BCQ while retaining the other existing comparators (v1 Table 1; v2 Table 3).

E3.justification: New protocols include 100-step SD v1.5/SDXL evaluations, explicit TFG/DAS compute allowances, and five-epoch distillation followed by verifier-free evaluation. CompBench difficulty estimation changes from eight random samples to four. ImageNet adds MSP evaluation and replaces the reported class-specific BFS temperatures with a temperature sweep (Appendices E.1–E.5).

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled BFS resampling/scoring/tempering ablations (Table 1), maze temperature and DFS-threshold sensitivity analyses (Table 8; Figure 7), and expanded local-versus-global scaling comparisons (Figure 4). The existing double-verifier analysis is extended to BFS, MSP measurements and adversarial examples. Policy-distillation training curves provide another new supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix E.1 newly specifies four-trial mean and standard-deviation reporting for ImageReward experiments. CompBench Figure 3 adds uncertainty bands and error bars absent from v1 Figure 4, although their meaning is not specified there. The existing five-seed D4RL protocol remains unchanged; these additions do not establish increased runs for retained results.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial ImageReward, baseline, sensitivity and distillation results. New D4RL comparator averages are 82.1 for TFG and 80.2 for DAS; distillation scores are 51.6, 98.8 and 86.3 (Tables 3–4). Maze/CompBench curves are replaced and ImageNet results gain BFS and MSP entries. Existing TTS D4RL scores and four/eight-particle ImageNet BoN FID/accuracy values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3.3 adds Theorem 1 and a Wasserstein convergence-bound proof under bounded-support, strong-log-concavity, smoothness and Lipschitz-Hessian assumptions. Sections C.3.1–C.3.2 also revise recurrence coefficients and explicitly incorporate verifier tempering into the annealed target. The original continuous-limit Proposition 1 is retained.

C1.justification: v1 emphasized a unified framework and efficient downstream search. v2 explicitly claims an improved BFS surpassing prior methods, the first adaptive DFS for diffusion inference scaling, and the first joint local/global scaling advancing the Pareto frontier (abstract and introduction). Expert iteration changes from a future direction into a demonstrated contribution.

C2.justification: v2 strengthens the central interpretation that global search is restricted to pretrained modes while local refinement can exceed base-model capabilities, and explains TFG saturation and DAS weaknesses through this distinction. It interprets higher MSP as reduced OOD generation. The hyperparameter-tuning limitation remains, but its proposed remedy changes from adaptive thresholds to evolutionary search.

D1.justification: Tables 6, 7 and 10 add BFS configurations, previously unspecified maze architecture/training parameters, and distillation settings; Appendix E.4.1 adds hardware and timing information. These maze disclosures do not establish an architecture change. Conversely, v2 omits v1's explicit ImageNet generator/resolution, complete class list, 100-step DDPM configuration and fixed local-search count.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix B substantially refocus positioning around particle-based search, tree search and gradient guidance. Added discussions include DAS, SVDD, TreeG, ABCD and EvoSearch, while Appendix D maps prior designs into the BFS framework. Much of v1's broader LLM expert-iteration and diffusion-application review is removed.

P1.justification: The introduction, contributions, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Global search now precedes local search, and experiments are reorganized from domain-based sections into BFS design, DFS adaptivity, joint scaling and reward hacking. The appendices are substantially restructured, beyond merely accommodating new scientific content.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn, including removal of the pruning panel. Maze and CompBench plots are redesigned; v1's appendix Ultra examples move into v2 Figure 5. New ablation, distillation and parameter tables and sensitivity plots are added. ImageNet curves and uncurated image grids are replaced by an expanded table and adversarial examples, alongside a document-template change.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important weakness in v1's efficiency evidence, which relied mainly on Best-of-N comparisons: competitive search baselines and controlled BFS and joint-scaling experiments substantially strengthen support for the central claims (Tables 1–3; Figure 4). It also tests policy distillation previously left as future work. Narrower benchmark reporting and lost ImageNet implementation details are drawbacks, but the stronger comparative and diagnostic evidence provides a clear substantial net gain.
